evidence.observation: get_parser(default_config_files, git_root) is the single declarative source of truth for option parsing. It constructs a configargparse.ArgumentParser with auto_env_var_prefix='AIDER_' (so every option is also readable from AIDER_-prefixed environment variables), config_file_parser_class=YAMLConfigFileParser and default_config_files supplied by the caller. It derives edit_format_choices dynamically from aider.coders.__all__ (lines 46-54) rather than hardcoding, and passes those choices to --edit-format/--chat-mode and --editor-edit-format. Arguments are partitioned into named add_argument_group blocks (Main model, API Keys and settings, Model settings, Cache settings, Repomap settings, History Files, Output settings, Git settings, Fixing and committing, Analytics, Upgrading, Modes, Voice settings, Other settings, Deprecated model settings), and several defaults are git_root-aware, e.g. --input-history-file/--chat-history-file (lines 271-288), --aiderignore with a type=lambda calling resolve_aiderignore_path (lines 426-432), --env-file via default_env_file (lines 800-805). It returns the parser; parsing itself happens in main().

resolve_aiderignore_path is the argparse type= coercion used for --aiderignore (args.py:429). It normalizes the user-supplied path at parse time: absolute paths are returned unchanged, relative paths are resolved against git_root when a git root is known, and otherwise left as-is relative to cwd. This is the clearest example of a default/type callback folding runtime context (git_root) into parsed option values, i.e. parsing and configuration are not fully separable.

default_env_file(git_root) returns os.path.join(git_root, '.env') when a git root exists else '.env'. It supplies the default for the --env-file option (args.py:803), so the .env file that main.py later loads via load_dotenv_files is anchored to the git root by default. Like resolve_aiderignore_path, it demonstrates context-derived defaults computed inside get_parser.

args.py's own main() is a documentation/completion helper, not the application entry point. It dispatches on sys.argv[1] to print Markdown help (get_md_help), a sample .env (get_sample_dotenv), a sample YAML config (get_sample_yaml), or a shtab shell-completion script. Each helper rebuilds the parser with get_parser([], None) and mutates parser.formatter_class, then calls argparse.ArgumentParser.format_help(parser) to render the same option definitions produced for runtime parsing. This confirms args.py owns the schema in one place, reused for both parsing and docs.

main() drives the whole parse -> validate -> runtime-config pipeline. It builds default_config_files in the order CWD/.aider.conf.yml, git-root/.aider.conf.yml, ~/.aider.conf.yml (lines 464-477), then does a two-pass parse: parse_known_args with the CWD-first list (line 481) inside a try that special-cases the AttributeError raised by a legacy 'yes:' config key via check_config_files_for_yes (lines 482-486); it reverses the list so home has lowest precedence, rebuilds the parser, and parses again (lines 494-498); it then loads dotenv files based on the parsed --env-file (line 501) and re-parses a third time with parse_args so values defined in .env become available (line 504). After parsing it maps parsed values onto runtime state: --shell-completions early-exits (506-510), --no-git forces args.git=False when the git module is absent (512-513), --no-verify-ssl rewires httpx and litellm globals (519-527), timeout/dark-mode/light-mode mutate args in place (529-544), and a large block of validation/interpretation follows: --set-env and --api-key split on '=' writing os.environ (589-610), API keys promoted to env vars (612-634), directory-vs-file argument validation (679-711), wrong-git-root recursion via guessed_wrong_repo (713-720), lint-command parsing via parse_lint_cmds with a None-means-error convention (885-888), model selection (777-783), model settings application (822-869), repo sanity check (924-927), and finally Coder.create(...) (973-1007) which is the concrete runtime configuration object. Coder.create's kwargs (map_refresh flipping to 'files' when caching at 954-955, stream forced off at 957-962, map_tokens defaulted from the model at 964-967) show post-parse derivation of effective runtime config.

check_config_files_for_yes scans each candidate config file for a line beginning with 'yes:' and emits a targeted migration message telling the user to use 'yes-always:'. It is invoked from the AttributeError handler around the first parse (main.py:482-486) because an unknown/legacy config key manifests as an AttributeError mentioning bool/object/has/no/attribute/strip. This is the validation stage that turns an otherwise opaque argparse failure into an actionable diagnostic.

get_git_root() uses git.Repo(search_parent_directories=True).working_tree_dir to guess the repo root before parsing, returning None on InvalidGitRepositoryError/FileNotFoundError. Its result is the git_root threaded into get_parser (main.py:479), which is why config-file discovery, history-file defaults, aiderignore resolution and .env defaults are all git-root anchored. It is later corrected after parsing by guessed_wrong_repo (main.py:716-720), which recurses into main() with force_git_root.

setup_git(git_root, io) is a post-validation runtime-configuration step gated on args.git (main.py:740-743). It returns early when the git module is unavailable, warns when run from the home directory, interactively offers to create a repo via make_new_repo, and fills in missing user.name/user.email defaults while warning the user. Its return value reassigns git_root, feeding check_gitignore and later GitRepo/Coder construction.

parse_lint_cmds converts the repeated --lint-cmd append values into a {language: command} dict. Inputs matching '^[a-z]+:.*' are split on the first colon into lang/cmd; anything else becomes lang=None. It reports malformed commands through io.tool_error/io.tool_output and returns None to signal failure, which main() interprets as a fatal error (main.py:885-888) before creating the coder. This is an explicit parse-time validation with a typed result consumed by Coder.create(lint_cmds=...).

generate_search_path_list builds the ordered, de-duplicated, absolute search path for per-user/per-repo config-ish files. The base order is home, git root, cwd-relative default_file, then an explicit command-line file; the list is resolved to absolute paths, reversed, de-duplicated, and reversed back so the command-line file wins and later entries override earlier ones. It is reused for both .aider.model.settings.yml (register_models) and .aider.model.metadata.json (register_litellm_models), and a variant feeds load_dotenv_files, so option values such as --model-settings-file select an override inserted at the front of the search list.

load_dotenv_files(git_root, dotenv_fname, encoding) computes the .env search path from generate_search_path_list, prepends ~/.aider/oauth-keys.env when present so OAuth keys load first (and can be overridden), then calls load_dotenv(fname, override=True) for each existing file and returns the loaded paths. It is called with the freshly parsed args.env_file and args.encoding (main.py:501), and because overrides are applied to os.environ, a third parse (main.py:504) can pick up options supplied only via .env. This closes the loop from option parsing back into environment-based configuration.

is_first_run_of_new_version records a (__version__, sys.executable) key in ~/.aider/installs.json and returns whether it was newly inserted, always returning False for '.dev' versions and True on any error. Its result is used by check_and_load_imports to decide between synchronous load_slow_imports and a background daemon thread (main.py:1226-1248), and by main() to decide whether to offer release notes (main.py:1099-1109). It is a runtime-configuration side channel derived from parsed args.verbose.

claims.claim: aider/args.py owns the complete option schema in a single function, get_parser, which returns a configargparse ArgumentParser configured with auto_env_var_prefix='AIDER_' and YAML config-file parsing; every runtime flag is declared there exactly once and grouped for help output.

Option defaults in args.py are not static: get_parser receives git_root and uses it to compute defaults for --aiderignore (resolve_aiderignore_path), --env-file (default_env_file), and the input/chat history files, so parsing already folds in runtime repository context.

The set of legal --edit-format choices is derived at parser construction time from the registered coder classes (aider.coders.__all__) rather than hardcoded, so validation of the option stays in sync with the available coder implementations.

aider/main.py's main() implements a deliberate multi-pass parse: parse_known_args to discover config-file/env context (with an AttributeError handler that calls check_config_files_for_yes to diagnose legacy 'yes:' keys), a rebuild after reversing config-file precedence, dotenv loading driven by the parsed --env-file, and a final parse_args that can incorporate options originating from .env.

Validation of user input is interleaved with configuration in main(): --set-env and --api-key entries must contain '=', file arguments must not mix a directory with other files, lint commands must parse into parse_lint_cmds' dict (None means fatal), and the repository passes sanity_check_repo; each failure emits an analytics exit event and returns a non-zero status instead of constructing a Coder.

The terminal runtime configuration is the kwargs dict passed to Coder.create at main.py:973-1007, and several values are derived after parsing rather than taken raw: map_refresh is forced to 'files' when --cache-prompts is set, args.stream is forced off when the model is not streaming, and map_tokens falls back to main_model.get_repo_map_tokens() when --map-tokens is None.

The git root is guessed before parsing (get_git_root) and re-guessed after parsing via guessed_wrong_repo; when the guess was wrong main() recurses with force_git_root so config-file locations, history files and the repo are all recomputed for the correct root.

The two files are coupled through a single parser object: main.py imports get_parser from aider.args, calls it with the computed default_config_files and git_root, and also passes that same parser instance into Commands (args=args, parser=parser), so parsing, help/format rendering, and in-chat reconfiguration all share one schema definition.

conclusion: aider/args.py and aider/main.py split responsibilities cleanly: args.py is the declarative, single-source schema (get_parser builds one configargparse.ArgumentParser with AIDER_ env-var prefix, YAML config files, dynamically derived edit-format choices, grouped options and git_root-aware defaults), while main.py is the imperative pipeline that consumes it. main() computes config-file precedence (CWD, git root, home), performs a multi-pass parse (parse_known_args -> dotenv load -> parse_args) so options can come from CLI, YAML config, env vars, or .env, validates and normalizes values (set-env/api-key splitting, lint-cmd parsing, directory/file rules, repo sanity, checklist of model settings), and then derives the effective runtime configuration, culminating in the Coder.create kwargs and a Commands object that retains the parser for later reconfiguration. The result is a clear parse -> validate -> configure flow in which args.py defines what is allowed and main.py decides what actually runs.
